newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still adrift late, stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still adrift late, stuck in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly remained down slightly late Tuesday in sluggish trade, but a fairly stable cash market kept prices bound in recent technical ranges, market sources said.
At 1405 EDT, August slipped 1.4 cents to $2.125 per million British thermal units, while September was 1.1 cents lower at $2.125. Other deferreds were steady to down slightly.

"Cash feels tight right now. We saw pretty decent demand today, particularly in Texas and Oklahoma. Chicago and the East are supposed to moderate, but the surprise is that the cash hasn't retraced," said one Texas-based trader.
Most agreed news early Tuesday that several nuclear units returned to full power lightly pressured the complex.
But they noted little conviction about market direction, adding activity was likely to remain slow this week due to the Independence Day holiday and some early-July industrial plant shutdowns.

Traders viewed revised 6-10 day forecasts as neutral, with heat expected to persist in the West and most of Texas, while the Midwest and Northeast should fluctuate around normal. Parts of the Southeast may be above-normal during the period.

Technically, traders still pegged August support along the up trendline at about $2.11 and then at the recent $2.08 low. Resistance was seen first at $2.15 and then along the trendline at $2.27. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA stock report range from 75-100 bcf versus a 93 bcf build last year.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices were unchanged to down slightly in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to slightly higher at about $2.03-2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted slightly lower in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
NYMEX said 9,912 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.
NYMEX natgas trade will close at 1300 EDT Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday Friday.
On the KCBT, August was unchanged at $2.02, while deferreds were still steady to one-half cent lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.4 cents to 10.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
